Troubleshooting

IPTV buffering? Try these fixes

Most buffering is caused by something between the router and the TV. Work down this list; most people are sorted by step four.

See plans from £7Ask for a free trial

Quick fixes

  1. Restart everything: router first, then the device, then the app.
  2. Test the speed on the TV device, not your phone. You want 10 Mbps for HD and 25 Mbps for 4K.
  3. Use a cable or powerline adapter if the router is in another room.
  4. Switch to the HD version of the channel if 4K stutters.
  5. Clear the app cache (Firestick: Settings → Applications → Manage installed applications).
  6. Change the player in the app settings (for example to VLC or ExoPlayer).
  7. Pause other big downloads such as game updates or cloud backups.
  8. Power the Firestick from the mains, not the TV’s USB port.
  9. Try a different DNS on the device or router.
  10. Update the app to the latest version.

IPTV not working at all?

If nothing loads, check your subscription has not expired, re-enter the login carefully (the server URL must be exact), and make sure you are not watching on more screens than your plan allows.

FAQ

Questions people ask

Why does IPTV buffer at weekends?

Everyone streams at once, so home Wi-Fi and broadband are under more pressure. A wired connection helps most.

Does a VPN fix buffering?

Sometimes, if your broadband provider slows video traffic, but a VPN can also slow things down. Try the steps above first.
